summary: Payroll AC-13 source-versioned statutory rulepack manifest validates official payroll/labor source refs, version labels, effective dates, approval evidence, source evidence refs, and digests for US federal and Korea examples while explicitly refusing calculation-engine, filing-rail, disbursement-rail, and cloud-deployment claims.

findings: The manifest is pure-domain provenance data with validation helpers, not a premature payroll calculation engine.
Official source URL allowlisting and source digest/evidence fields prevent anonymous or mutable rulepack provenance.
Rulepack source manifests create a stable input contract for later cloud calculation/filing services without bundling those capabilities now.
Capability booleans make calculation, filing, disbursement, and cloud deployment non-claims mechanically testable.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if sources are empty, source versions are missing, source refs are unsafe, official URLs are not allowlisted, or calculation/filing/disbursement/cloud booleans are overclaimed.
findings: Positive US/KR manifest coverage and negative overclaim/unofficial-source validation are both covered.
Future calculation adapters can consume PayrollStatutoryRulepackManifest rather than re-discovering official source provenance requirements.
Focused payroll domain tests/clippy, payroll package-group tests/clippy, 25-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan passed.

F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The manifest proves official source provenance before calculation logic can claim correctness.
rejected_reasons: Tax calculation requires jurisdiction-specific annual tables and much broader statutory test fixtures beyond this slice.
A bare rulepack ref cannot prove which official sources, versions, and digests were used.

findings: No secrets, network calls, storage, filing credentials, disbursement rails, or provider SDK are introduced.
Source refs, official URLs, evidence refs, and version labels reject unsafe path/credential-shaped metadata.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Manifest validation loops over a small source vector and performs string validation only; no I/O or runtime path exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, or calculation hot path is introduced.

data_class_touched: PUBLIC official source URLs and capability flags
findings: IRS Publication 15 and 15-T are represented as source-versioned inputs, not hard-coded rates.
DOL/MOEL/Law.go.kr sources are allowlisted as official provenance refs while filing and calculation remain non-claims.
The change is additive within the payroll domain and tests; no storage migration, external resource, or API deployment is introduced.
Manifest records source_count, evidence refs, digests, official URLs, retrieved_at timestamps, and schema version for future audit dashboards.
Runtime audit-chain emission remains a non-claim; branch evidence appends static audit-chain rows only.
Payroll AC-13 and D-12 define the migration seam from static rulepack provenance to future calculation/filing adapters.
Existing trial-close behavior continues to consume rulepack refs while this slice deepens source provenance for future slices.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: Payroll calculation correctness should not be claimed until official annual source provenance is modeled and tested.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: CS-ENT-PAYROLL-005 rulepack_manifest tests and official IRS/DOL/MOEL/Law.go.kr source refs
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Future calculation engines could claim correctness from opaque rulepack names without evidence of which official source versions were consumed.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: The current payroll trial close already validates rulepack refs; the missing prerequisite is richer source provenance, not changing close behavior.

findings: This advances corporate payroll toward cloud-grade statutory calculation/filing readiness while preserving honest non-claims.
Names follow Payroll statutory rulepack/source manifest vocabulary.
Payroll spec, plan, todo, evidence, and audit-chain references were updated.
Pure payroll domain types/functions and domain tests carry the feature; app/API/runtime/storage crates are untouched.
No tax calculation engine, filing rail, disbursement rail, cloud adapter, storage adapter, listener, or runtime audit emitter was introduced.
No third-party dependencies were added.
No wire API schema is changed; this is a Rust domain contract only.
Validation uses existing identifier/ref/digest/date/period helpers plus official-source URL allowlisting and explicit overclaim refusal.
